title: U.S. House · Iowa's 3rd District
area: South-central Iowa, including Des Moines and its suburbs

context.text: Incumbent Zach Nunn (R) advanced unopposed from the June 2, 2026 Republican primary. Sarah Trone Garriott (D), a member of the Iowa State Senate, defeated Jennifer Konfrst, Tracy Limon, and Easton Wolfe in the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary. Cook Political Report rated the district R+2.

summary.text: Nunn is the Republican incumbent for Iowa's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2022. He is a colonel in the U.S. Air Force Reserve and former National Security Council staffer who previously served in the Iowa Senate and Iowa House.

background.text: Nunn served in the U.S. Air Force and is a colonel in the Air Force Reserve.

He earned a bachelor's degree in political science and international relations from Drake University (2002), a master's degree in military operational art and science from the U.S. Air Force Air Command and Staff College, and a master's degree in international relations and national security studies from Cambridge University (2007).

His career includes working as an adjunct professor in cybersecurity and national policy at Drake University, a director of business development with SimSpace Corporation, chief operations officer and national counterintelligence officer with the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, and director of cybersecurity policy and engagement on the White House National Security Council.
Before his 2022 election to the U.S. House, Nunn served four years each in the Iowa Senate and the Iowa House of Representatives.

priorities.text: Improving the economy, supporting Iowa agriculture, holding government accountable, keeping the country safe, and helping families and kids, according to his official House issues page.
Says tax relief on tips and overtime income and expanded small-business deductions are helping Iowa workers keep more of their pay and giving manufacturers certainty to invest and hire.
Government accountability, including leading the bipartisan Stop Insider Trading Act to ban members of Congress and their immediate families from trading individual stocks while in office.
priorities.quote: Banning stock trades in Congress is about accountability, and every American should demand it from their elected officials.

positions.summary: Highlighted a 2025 spending bill's $150 billion in new border and immigration funding, citing more border patrol agents, expanded detention capacity, and additional surveillance technology as wins he helped secure.
positions.quote: Today, we passed $150 billion in new funding to deliver serious backup for our law enforcement, border agents, and military.

positions.summary: Says he has championed the Israel Security Supplemental Appropriations Act to replenish Israel's Iron Dome missile defense system and助 assist Israel militarily.
positions.quote: Championing the Israel Security Supplemental Appropriations Act to replenish the Iron Dome and assist our strongest ally in the Middle East as they fight Hamas and other militant groups.

record.text: Served on the House Committee on Agriculture (Commodity Markets, Digital Assets, and Rural Development; General Farm Commodities, Risk Management, and Credit subcommittees) and the Committee on Financial Services (Capital Markets; National Security, Illicit Finance, and International Financial Institutions subcommittees), 2023-2024.
Led the Stop Insider Trading Act, which the House passed 232-198, to prohibit members of Congress and their immediate family members from buying individual stocks while serving in office.

candidates.name: Sarah Trone Garriott
candidates.currentRole: Member, Iowa State Senate, District 14 (since 2023); previously District 22 (2021-2023)

summary.text: Trone Garriott is a Democratic member of the Iowa State Senate representing District 14, an ordained Lutheran minister, and a former interfaith and food-bank-network coordinator, challenging Nunn for this seat.

background.text: Born in Minneapolis, Minnesota, she graduated from Cloquet High School and earned a B.A. in history from the College of St. Scholastica (1999), an M.A. in theological studies from Harvard University Divinity School (2003), and an M.Div. from the Lutheran School of Theology at Chicago (2008).

Her career includes working as a coordinator of interfaith engagement with the Des Moines Area Religious Council, an associate pastor of Faith Lutheran Church in Clive, Iowa, and a pastor of Martin Luther Evangelical Lutheran Church in Bergton, Virginia. She co-founded the Iowa Interfaith Exchange.

She has represented Iowa Senate District 14 since January 2023, after representing District 22 from 2021 to 2023, winning re-election in both 2022 and 2024 in a competitive, Republican-leaning district.

priorities.text: A higher standard for Washington, growing the economy by investing in people rather than special interests, and making life more affordable.
Affordable health care, protecting public schools, and protecting Iowa's land, water, and clean energy future.

positions.summary: Trone Garriott's campaign issues page lists "Reproductive freedom is personal—and non-negotiable" as one of her core issues.
Trone Garriott's campaign issues page lists "Protecting Iowa's land, water, and clean energy future" as a priority.

record.text: Serves on the Iowa Senate Education, Commerce, Health and Human Services, Natural Resources & Environment, and Health Policy Oversight committees (2025-2026).

researchNotes: Nunn's official issues page and Trone Garriott's campaign issues page present their priorities as category headings without expanded text in the fetched page content, so detail beyond the listed issue names was not available within the research budget. No 2025-2026 committee assignment listing was found for Nunn on Ballotpedia; only his 2023-2024 assignments are recorded here. Nunn's official-site press releases (2026) and Ballotpedia biography were checked for statements matching the guide's 15 issue categories; none directly addressed abortion, guns, immigration, climate, taxes on high earners, or the other issue statements, so no positions were added for him beyond the priorities above.
